text.title: pnpm-package-management Procedure
text.summary: Six-step procedure taking a repo from whatever package manager it has today to a pinned, guarded, reproducible pnpm setup.

step.name: audit-current-state
step.action: Record what is there: `package-lock.json`, `yarn.lock`, existing `.npmrc` settings, current `packageManager` field, and any native add-ons (`sharp`, `node-canvas`, `better-sqlite3`) that historically forced hoisting.
step.output: Audit note listing what to remove and what to add

step.name: pin-package-manager
step.action: Add `"packageManager": "pnpm@x.y.z"` to the root package.json, then `corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@x.y.z --activate`.
step.reference: Bootstrap script doing the pin plus the initial install.

step.name: emit-npmrc
step.action: Write `.npmrc` with `strict-peer-dependencies=true`, `auto-install-peers=true`, `prefer-frozen-lockfile=true`, `engine-strict=true`. Leave `shamefully-hoist` unset so it stays false.
step.decision-gate: If a native add-on genuinely cannot resolve, use `node-linker=hoisted` with an inline comment naming the add-on and linking the upstream issue — never `shamefully-hoist=true`.

step.name: block-other-managers
step.action: Add `"preinstall": "npx -y only-allow pnpm"` to scripts. Delete `package-lock.json` and `yarn.lock`. Commit `pnpm-lock.yaml`.
step.output: Guarded root package.json and a single lockfile

step.name: wire-ci
step.action: Use `pnpm/action-setup` at the version matching the `packageManager` pin, run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, and cache the pnpm store keyed on the lockfile hash. In a monorepo, scope build and test with `--filter '...[origin/main]'`.
step.reference: Workflow with corepack, store cache and the frozen-lockfile gate.

step.name: validate
step.input: Artefact metadata describing the resulting setup
step.action: Run the validator against it and fix every violation before committing. Land the lockfile change as its own commit, separate from application code.
step.decision-gate: If the validator returns non-zero, halt and fix — do not commit a partially converted setup, which is the state that produces two lockfiles.
